rationale: A wins because it understands the real trade story is not the financing confetti; it is whether three utilities will put their names and grid pain on the record. "Verdano's three utility pilots are the story its funding round isn't" is the right wedge, while B literally refuses the same vein with "A customer-story with no named customer and no independently verified result gives a trade reporter nothing to report." B is cleaner than most slop machines, but it is too timid and leaves the strongest reporter path on the floor.
gaps_in_A: "community solar breaks the grid before rooftop does" invents a rooftop comparison the update never gives. Good tension, unsupported headline.
"the community-solar bottleneck is software, not panels" is a sharp category thesis, but the update does not prove it. A mostly repairs this in the proof section, but the headline outruns the facts.
"Not for grid-ops trade press, which does not care where founders used to work" is too absolute. Some trade reporters would care if the NREL/Tesla link explains technical credibility.
gaps_in_B: "Three utilities are already paying for community-solar AI" is refused as `no_journalist_shape`, but that is the strongest trade angle if one utility can be named or even credibly characterized. B throws away the best material, then asks for the same named utility under its category angle.
"The seed round is live now" is invented. The update gives current time, not announcement status, embargo timing, or publication date.

"the founder-profile angle is pitchable now on the facts in hand" is overconfident. Ex-Tesla Energy and ex-NREL without founder names, roles, dates, or a real founding anecdote is a thin people story.

B misses the skeptical procurement story entirely: "14-person startup," "plans to hire 10 engineers," "three paying utility customers in pilot," and "no revenue figure" create a real tension reporters can test.
